label: no
controls_available: The exact difficulty-2 profile is a 9-by-9 map with 81 parcels, 6 boundary-warp steps, 4 displaced parcels, a 9-parcel-change budget, one-household population tolerance, and one two-parcel balanced exchange.
Click a visible parcel polygon to select it.
Click one of the nine visible canton-seal buttons to assign the selected parcel to that canton; a changed assignment costs one parcel change.
Click UNDO to reverse the last assignment and restore the prior assignment state.
Click CERTIFY CHARTER to submit the current assignment; certification is administrative.
The simplified surface has no brush or drag control; the full-mode brush requirements are inactive here.
autonomous_processes: No autonomous task-state process or autonomous outcome phase occurs between agent actions; the generated parcels, guild marks, adjacency, and initial assignment remain fixed.
The mechanic has only action-triggered CSS fill, hover, selection, and button transitions; these are presentation effects and do not change assignment, control availability, or grading state.

The shared runtime can advance its virtual clock and service registered timers or animation frames, but this mechanic registers no timer, animation loop, physics process, or clock-dependent state update.
grouped_control_modes: D_assign: every simplified parcel-selection followed by canton-proxy assignment occurrence across seeds and attempts; the canton assignment is the outcome-affecting action.
D_undo: every undo-button reversal of the most recent assignment.
Certification is an administrative submission and is excluded from outcome-affecting D.

clause_i.reason: For the assignment mode, waiting leaves the same board and the same assignment opportunity available, so an observation-free defer/no-op policy can remain optimal at the delayed boundary; the static task does not force an observation-dependent action choice.

clause_ii.reason: A zero-length bounded window containing the current screenshot exposes the parcel geometry, current canton colors, guild house marks, visible seals, and the population/holding rules. Those visible facts are sufficient for a screenshot-only static partition plan; no chronological frame sequence is needed.

clause_iii.reason: No autonomous task-state change occurs for any legitimate D, so no available assignment or undo action becomes unavailable or strictly less effective during a positive delay while success remains possible. The CSS transitions do not affect the graded state, and any loss from the 240-second allowance would be deadline-only, which the definition excludes.

common_visible_process: None. There is no visible autonomous process whose evolution could be the common witness for clauses (i), (ii), and (iii).

pre_run.reason: The generator materializes the initial and target partitions before play, and the simplified UI requires outcome-affecting parcel assignments during the run. There is no autonomous outcome phase that can start after preparation and then run without further outcome-affecting actions, so the pre-run threshold is not met. No percentage is asserted. This does not change the already mathematical No label.

source_evidence.claim: The frozen definition requires non-clock autonomous task-state evolution to cause strict loss of an action opportunity; static tasks, deadline-only effects, and unrelated animations do not qualify.
Difficulty 2 is the 9-by-9, four-displacement, nine-change, one-exchange profile; simplified interaction is click-through-proxy and the configured observation window is 0 ms with one frame.
The generator constructs target and initial assignments during generation, then returns fixed public parcels/adjacency/initial assignment and private truth; there is no post-start state process.
Rendering evaluates the current assignment; simplified input selects a parcel and the canton button records the assignment, while undo restores history and certify only posts the replay payload.
The mechanic stylesheet contains presentation transitions and hover/selection styling but no task animation or time-driven state behavior.
The grader replays only the submitted visible assignment/undo events, checks the final partition and metrics, and applies the simplified input-surface contract without reading task time.
The verifier loads the exported result and invokes the independent charter replay grader; it adds no temporal task behavior.
The shared clock advances only registered timers/animation callbacks or commanded run windows; the charter mechanic registers none of those task-state callbacks.
The browser runtime dynamically loads the charter mechanic and dispatches the fetched static state to it; the generic main path contains no charter-specific autonomous update.

The simplified solver uses a visible parcel click followed by a visible canton-button click for each repair and certifies after the static repairs; its private target reads are solver evidence, not policy information.
